captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 5. In this lesson: Why the sea is salty.
Understand how a myth explains something in nature.
Here are some new words. Myth. An old story that explains something in nature. Legend.
An old story about a hero that may be partly true. Magic.
A special power that makes impossible things happen. Listen and say them. myth
legend
magic.
And some more words. Greedy. Wanting much more than you need. Grind.
Crush something into very small pieces. Sink. Go down under the water. Listen and say them.
greedy
grind
sink.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: an old story that explains something in nature?
Now some grammar: Past perfect. Use had, plus the past participle,
for an action that happened before another action in the past.
For example: When we arrived, the film had started.
For example: She had lost the key, so she couldn't open the door.
Now listen, and read along. Why the sea is salty. Long ago, the sea was sweet like rain.
In those days a poor fisherman owned a small magic mill.
If he said, ‘Grind, mill, grind!’, it made anything he wanted.
A greedy sea captain heard about the mill and stole it one night.
He had already loaded his ship with fish, and he wanted salt to keep it fresh.
Far out at sea he shouted, ‘Grind, mill, grind salt!’ The mill began to pour out salt.
But the captain had never learned the words to stop it.
The salt filled the deck, then the cabin, and the ship sank to the bottom of the sea.
And there the mill still grinds today – which is why the sea is salty.
Another question. The video will stop. What was the sea like long ago, in the myth?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like myth, legend, magic.
You practised the past perfect. And you read Why the sea is salty.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 5. In this lesson: The hero's journey.
Identify the parts of a legend: setting, problem, journey, climax and ending.
Here are some new words. Hero. A brave person people admire. Quest.
A long search for something important. Challenge. A difficult thing to do.
Listen and say them. hero
quest
challenge.
And some more words. Climax. The most exciting part of a story. Reward.
Something you get for doing something good. Village elder.
An old and respected person in a village. Listen and say them. climax
reward
village elder.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: a brave person people admire?
Now some grammar: Story structure words.
Writers use time and sequence words to move a story forward: at first, soon, meanwhile,
at last, in the end. For example: At first, nobody believed her.
For example: At last, she reached the mountain.
Now listen, and read along. Amara and the river dragon.
In a village by the mountains, the river had stopped flowing.
The fields were dry and the people were thirsty.
The village elder said, ‘A dragon sleeps in the river's cave.
Only someone brave can wake it.’ At first, nobody spoke.
Then a girl called Amara stepped forward. For three days Amara climbed.
She crossed a bridge of ice and found her way through a dark forest.
Meanwhile, the villagers waited and hoped. At last she reached the cave.
The dragon was lying across the river like a huge wall. Amara did not fight it.
Instead, she sang a gentle song. The dragon opened its golden eyes, stretched and moved aside.
The water rushed down the mountain.
In the end, Amara returned home as a hero, and every year the village sings her song.
Another question. The video will stop. What was the problem in the village?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like hero, quest, challenge.
You practised story structure words. And you read Amara and the river dragon.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
